steps.outcome: Read the earlier agent's transcript and scratch state. All of its host jobs (1054-1057) had finished and nothing from the dry run was queued (squeue showed only S1a's held 1051/1053). I fetched the one output it never collected (glmm-harness-secondary.json, receipt-1054) and the rescore-a0a, pyrep and slurm logs into scratch s1a-dry-run/host-fetch/. The host's src-d5f5798 matches the local d5f5798 export: the combined SHA-256 of harness/q2_stage1, the sbatch, the GLMM Dockerfile, the plan renderer, plan-a0a.json and the registration is 2031174e... on both.

git archive d5f5798 to s1a-dry-run/export, uv venv in s1a-dry-run/venv (Python 3.13, numpy 2.5.2, scipy 1.18.0). tests/test_q2_stage1_{analysis,records_rules,estimators,glmm,rescore}.py: 46 passed, 1 skipped. steps.step: Synthetic A1 data, 8 scenarios (earlier agent, sim/simulate.py)
steps.outcome: Every base and extension slot comes from plan.a1_slots, run through the real lane objects (Dispatcher, re-queue, fill rule, USR1 cut, receipts) on a simulated clock at V=20 and T_A1=110. Records follow the driver schema, and rescoring rows follow rescore_episode's shape. Scenarios: null, harness (beta 0.8, sd_th 1.2), session (session shift, 4B H-GA truncation 30%, slow S2 4B cut by USR1, GPU end forgotten by Slurm, more and double losses), floor (4B at the floor, every job above the high price), dr0 (DR0 fires after A1-9B-S1), dr0late (DR0 fires at A1-9B-S2, so 4B has S1 only), baseincomplete (DR0 fires on A1-4B-S2), fractional (fractional base scores). All of them include metric exceptions, postconfig 5xx and no-reply cases, and re-queued losses.

steps.step: Registered CLI pipeline per scenario (earlier agent, sim/run_pipeline.sh)
steps.outcome: Commands run: rules dr0 per job, rescore merge per job, cat into a1.jsonl, analysis costs, analysis --records/--plan/--costs. Reports came out for null, harness, session, floor, dr0late and baseincomplete. The report crashed for dr0 (TypeError in rules.dr5) and fractional (ValueError). DR0 exited 3 exactly where it was built to fire. The 'session' costs step first crashed only because the simulator wrote a relative bridge_dir; after a sim fix it fell back to the bridge's stopped.json as registered. DR1, DR2, DR4, DR5, P1-P5, the D56 postconfig sensitivity (episodes_missing), the metric-exception, flagged-task and secondary sets, the truncation label (session: 4B labelled at 0.307), the per-session cells and attempts, the cost card and the 'not externally anchored' label all appear.

Recomputed by hand for harness, session and baseincomplete: delta, D_b and D_w per size, X per size and pi per size. All match the report. Cell counts per (size, harness, session) for final records and for attempts had 0 mismatches (null, session). The postconfig-missing count matched (4 and 27). Per-job episodes and GPU-h per episode matched costs.json.

steps.step: Report on host Python (earlier agent, CPU-only Slurm 1056)
steps.outcome: Host system python3 3.10.12 with numpy 1.21.5 and scipy 1.8.0 ran the null report in 21 s. It is byte-identical to the Mac venv report (sha256 f6a60f1a...). Job 1055 had failed at once only because sbatch --wrap runs /bin/sh (a 'Bad substitution' in the dry-run's own wrapper).

steps.outcome: All 8 fits exited 0. null, harness, session, dr0late and baseincomplete primaries: both fits converged with pdHess true. harness-secondary (1,664 episodes, 104 tasks): converged, task:harness LRT p 0.0022 (boundary-corrected 0.0011), share CI [0.036, 0.152]. floor: both fits pdHess false, LRT null, yet the bootstrap still ran (134/200 refits not converged, all 200 used). dr0 (9B only): both fits report the error 'contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels', handled gracefully. Run times: 12-14 min per primary, 19 min secondary, 8 in parallel on 8 CPUs.

steps.outcome: rescore capture exited 0 after 508 s. 20 rows, live_offline_match 20/20, corrected_applies 4, no *_error. I then checked locally: the 20 real A0a records validate under records.read_jsonl, rescore.merge with those rows sets corrected_score on 20/20 (0 corrected flips), and analysis.gpu_elapsed reads the real A0a receipt (364 s, source 'scontrol EndTime'). steps.outcome: All 256 steps carry processed_sha256, messages_sha256, ir_sha256 and prompt_sha256. analysis.divergence_summary gives within: environment 7, serving 3 (between: none, since A0a has one session). steps.step: Repros re-run on the frozen code (this agent, sim/repros_v2.py; output in sim/repros_v2.out)
steps.outcome: All confirmed on d5f5798. F1: a fractional base score crashes the report. F2: only A1-9B-S1 present crashes it at rules.py:250; on an all-NaN statistic x_signflip_p returns 1/(n+1)=0.000999. F3: with 4B in one session, session_signflip_p[4B] is 0.000999 while session_shift_4B is None, pi_small==pi_9B but is labelled 'mean of pi_4B and pi_9B', and M is 0.13. F4: without --costs the report has no DR4 or cost card and P5 reads not falsified. F5: when rescoring is absent or failed, the corrected delta equals the primary delta with no coverage field. F6: main() never passes step_logs, so first_divergence is never in the report. F7: section 15 items are missing (see bug 6). F8: glmm.py accepts only 'synthetic'.

steps.step: Section 15 audit against the report's keys (this agent)
steps.outcome: Present: primary and secondary estimands (raw), corrected estimands on the base only, per domain (base, raw), DR1, DR2, DR4, DR5, the DR-A label, P1-P5, losses by type and cell over finals and attempts per (size, harness), (size, session) and (size, harness, session), observation counts, postconfig replies, failures and server errors (server errors also by step type), the metric-exception, postconfig and flagged sensitivities, truncation shares and label plus the mediator delta, exposure strata and delta, checker-input discordance, live-vs-offline mismatches, corrected flips, the fractional count and sensitivity (when it does not crash), and the cost card by job, size and harness. Missing: see bugs 5 and 6.

bugs.where: harness/q2_stage1/analysis.py:454 (report: fractional_score = E.delta(R.outcome_array(finals, base, value="score"))) together with harness/q2_stage1/estimators.py:47-48 (_check)
bugs.what: One scored base episode with a score strictly between 0 and 1 crashes the whole registered report. The fractional-score sensitivity passes raw scores into estimators that accept only 0, 1 or NaN, so the report exits 1 ('outcomes must be 0, 1 or NaN') and writes no report.json.
bugs.repro: cd s1a-dry-run/export && PYTHONPATH=. ../venv/bin/python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tests'); import test_q2_stage1_analysis as T; from harness.q2_stage1 import analysis as A; r=T.synthetic(0.3,0.3,1); i=next(k for k,x in enumerate(r) if x['task_id']=='b00' and x['status']=='scored'); r[i]['score']=0.83; A.report(r,T.PLAN,n_boot=20,n_rand=20)" -> ValueError at estimators.py:48 <- analysis.py:454. Through the CLI: scenario 'fractional', data/fractional/analysis/report.err, exit 1.
bugs.would_affect_real_analysis: Yes, if any base episode scores fractionally. Three base tasks have continuous metrics in the pinned OSWorld: fba2c100 and 47f7c0ce (compare_images, raw SSIM with no reference_base_result) and c59742c0 (compare_audios, exp(-DTW distance)). Any saved output that is not identical to gold scores between 0 and 1; the driver turns only out-of-range scores into metric exceptions. Every registered output (DR2, DR5, P1-P5, RESULTS) would then be blocked. The code is frozen, so any workaround is a recorded deviation. This is unknowable before the run without reading outcomes.

bugs.what: If DR0 fires after the first A1 job, so only A1-9B-S1 records exist, the report crashes ('>' between NoneType and float), although the registration says data already collected are reported as incomplete. Second, signflip_p returns (0+1)/(nflip+1) when the statistic is all-NaN: x_signflip_p gives 0.000999 on such data, which DR2 would read as 'Present'.
bugs.repro: F2 in sim/repros_v2.py: report on [x for x in T.synthetic(0.3,0.3,2) if x['job']=='A1-9B-S1'] -> TypeError at rules.py:250 <- analysis.py:163. E.x_signflip_p(y, 1000, default_rng(42)) on the same y -> 0.000999. Through the CLI: scenario 'dr0', report.err exit 1. The GLMM on these data fails gracefully ('contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels').
bugs.would_affect_real_analysis: The crash path cannot happen now: both S1 jobs passed DR0 (D57). The all-NaN p-value mechanism still matters through bug 3.

bugs.what: When a size has only one session (DR0 fires at A1-9B-S2 so A1-4B-S2 never runs, or 4B-S2 is lost), the report runs but its output is wrong-looking. session_signflip_p for that size is 0.000999, a spurious 'significant' session shift, while session_shift is None. pi_small silently becomes pi_9B but stays labelled 'mean of pi_4B and pi_9B', and DR5 compares it with M_SMALL 0.13 instead of the 0.18 the registration ties to a pi_9B-only share. DR1 is read on 4B's session-1 data alone. Nothing labels the output incomplete, and when DR0 fires on the last job (scenario baseincomplete) the report still prints DR2 and DR5 with no incomplete label.
bugs.repro: F3 in sim/repros_v2.py (records without A1-4B-S2) -> {'session_shift_4B': None, 'session_signflip_p': [0.000999, 0.170829], 'pi_4B': None, 'DR1': False, 'pi_small_rule': 'mean of pi_4B and pi_9B', 'pi_small==pi_9B': True, 'DR5_M': 0.13}. Through the CLI: data/dr0late/analysis/report.json (session_signflip_p [0.0001, 0.405], D_b_4B None, DR5 M 0.13).
bugs.would_affect_real_analysis: Yes, if DR0 fires for either session-2 job, neither of which has run yet. The operator would have to choose by hand how to report DR1, DR2 and DR5 and the session test, and how to label the data incomplete.

bugs.what: Offline rescoring is serial: each scoring is a fresh spawned process, about 10.6 s each, so about 25 s per episode. capture opens --out with 'w', so it cannot resume. It silently skips scored episodes that have no capture.json. A worker error or timeout leaves corrected=None, merge writes corrected_score None, and outcome_array then falls back to the live score. The report carries no count of rescoring coverage or errors.
bugs.repro: Job 1057: 20 A0a episodes (48 worker runs) took 508 s. F5 in sim/repros_v2.py: rows with corrected None and corrected_error set -> 224 merged records with corrected_score None, checker_corrected delta == primary delta, no coverage field.
bugs.would_affect_real_analysis: Yes. Each A1 job has about 452 episodes (D57), so about 3 h of serial rescoring per job, above the s1a-cpu.sbatch 2 h default. Without a --time override the job hits TIMEOUT and leaves a partial file. Missing or failed rescoring would silently turn the corrected (secondary) verdicts into raw ones. The operator must choose the time limit and parallelism, and must count coverage by hand.

bugs.where: harness/q2_stage1/analysis.py:635-674 (main) vs analysis.py:478-479; registration section 15 and section 9 item 11

runbook:
Registered S1a analysis, frozen code d5f5798. Run on the host only after A1-4B-S2 has left the queue and its DR0 has been read, and only while no S1a job is pending or running (D58). Everything runs from the read-only export, CPU only, with no GRES. Poll long jobs with short commands; no command should block more than 5 minutes.

ssh -o BatchMode=yes fal-h100-01
R=~host/cotcodec-runs/stage0/q2-stage1
X=$R/src/d5f57988ab94e0c098feddb744b78b73b5ad88ca
PLAN=$X/program/evidence/2026-10-09/q2-stage1-prefreeze/plan/plan-a0a.json
A=$R/analysis/s1a-v1                 # new directory, write-once
VMS="1045 1048 1051 <VM_A1_4B_S2>"    # A1-9B-S1, A1-4B-S1, A1-9B-S2, A1-4B-S2 (registered order)
mkdir -p $A && cd $X

# 0. Preconditions
squeue -h -o '%i %j %T'            # nothing from S1a pending or running
sha256sum $PLAN                    # expect a5f0aadce1208d9d9ab31ff572ca93e624dbd87e1b50dd194987ff8cc46e1806
python3 -E -s -B -c "import json;from pathlib import Path;from harness.q2_stage1 import lane,plan as P;print(lane.frozen_registration(Path('.'))['sha256']);p=json.load(open('$PLAN'));assert P.digest({k:v for k,v in p.items() if k!='plan_sha256'})==p['plan_sha256']=='6a3f0219448301d95a80d443ed75892eaac093e42349ef98fb985a5d87467d51'"
# the registration sha must print f9db7cc38c4954b3144ac5a1afaf7bf5366449081b06c80bf89888bdf653afd8

# 1. DR0 for every A1 job (the report does not carry DR0; exit 3 means fired)
for VM in $VMS; do python3 -E -s -B -m harness.q2_stage1.rules dr0 --run-dir $R/runs/$VM --plan $PLAN > $A/dr0-$VM.json; echo "$VM exit=$?" >> $A/dr0-exits.txt; done
# If DR0 fired anywhere, label every output 'incomplete'. If a size has a single session, do not read its session_signflip_p, the pi_small label, or DR5's M from the report (bug 3).

# 2. Offline rescoring: one CPU-only Slurm job per run directory, in the metric image (as job 1057).
#    About 25 s per episode serial, so about 3 h per 452-episode job: override the 2 h default.
IMGM=sha256:2006c1a9247e4911a82508cd22e9d9a7efc5c13e35a20e8a03baac7112876230
HEXM=$(python3 -c 'import json;print(json.dumps(["/opt/venv-lock/bin/python","-m","harness.q2_stage1.rescore","capture","--run-dir","/ro/run","--osworld","/inputs/OSWorld","--file-cache","/inputs/file_cache_1e112283/files","--out","/out/rescored.jsonl"]).encode().hex())')
for VM in $VMS; do mkdir -p $A/rescore-$VM; sbatch --parsable --time=08:00:00 --export=ALL,Q2M_MODE=run,Q2M_IMAGE_ID=$IMGM,Q2M_ARGV_JSON_HEX=$HEXM,Q2M_SOURCE=$X,Q2M_RUN_DIR=$A/rescore-$VM,Q2M_INPUTS=~host/cotcodec-runs/stage0/q2-evaluator-mutation/inputs,Q2M_EXTRA_RO=$R/runs/$VM:/ro/run $X/infra/slurm/host-single-node/s1a-cpu.sbatch; done
# Poll: squeue -h -j <ids>; cat $A/rescore-*/receipt-*.json  (exit_status 0 expected)
# Coverage check (reads no outcome): scored records vs rows, and rows with *_error
for VM in $VMS; do python3 -E -s -B -c "import json,sys;e=[json.loads(l) for l in open(sys.argv[1]) if l.strip()];r=[json.loads(l) for l in open(sys.argv[2]) if l.strip()];print(sys.argv[3],'scored',sum(x['status']=='scored' for x in e),'rows',len(r),'errors',sum(any(k.endswith('_error') for k in x) for x in r))" $R/runs/$VM/episodes.jsonl $A/rescore-$VM/rescored.jsonl $VM; done

# 3. Merge corrected scores per job, then build one analysis record file
for VM in $VMS; do python3 -E -s -B -m harness.q2_stage1.rescore merge --episodes $R/runs/$VM/episodes.jsonl --rescored $A/rescore-$VM/rescored.jsonl --out $A/merged-$VM.jsonl; done
for VM in $VMS; do cat $A/merged-$VM.jsonl; done > $A/a1.jsonl
sha256sum $PLAN $A/a1.jsonl $A/merged-*.jsonl $R/runs/*/episodes.jsonl > $A/inputs.sha256

# 4. Cost card input. Run on the host: receipts name absolute host bridge dirs.
python3 -E -s -B -m harness.q2_stage1.analysis costs $(for VM in $VMS; do printf -- '--run-dir %s ' $R/runs/$VM; done) --out $A/costs.json

# 5. The registered report. No --anchor or --public: ANCHOR-UNAVAILABLE.
#    About 20 s on host python3 (3.10.12, numpy 1.21.5, scipy 1.8.0); byte-identical to a uv venv run.
python3 -E -s -B -m harness.q2_stage1.analysis --records $A/a1.jsonl --plan $PLAN --costs $A/costs.json --out $A/report.json; echo "exit=$?"
# exit 1 with 'outcomes must be 0, 1 or NaN' means a fractional base score (bug 1): stop and record a deviation; do not patch the frozen code.

# 6. First divergence. Step logs stay on the host and there is no registered entry point; state the choices made (base tasks, scored final records, final attempt).
python3 -E -s -B -c "import json,sys;from pathlib import Path;from harness.q2_stage1 import analysis as A,records as R;p=json.load(open('$PLAN'));base=set(p['base']);f=R.final_records(R.read_jsonl(Path('$A/a1.jsonl')));runs=[Path('$R/runs')/v for v in '$VMS'.split()];logs={}
for k,r in f.items():
  if r['status']!='scored' or k[2] not in base: continue
  n=str(r['slot']).replace(':','_')+'.a'+str(r['attempt'])
  for d in runs:
    q=d/'episodes'/n/'steps.jsonl'
    if q.is_file(): logs[k]=[json.loads(x) for x in q.read_text().splitlines() if x.strip()]; break
print(json.dumps({'step_logs':len(logs),'first_divergence':A.divergence_summary(logs)},indent=1))" > $A/first-divergence.json

# 7. GLMM (secondary model). glmm.py has no command for real input, so write it with the registered functions: primary = base; secondary = base plus the completed blocks.
mkdir -p $A/glmm-inputs $A/glmm-out
python3 -E -s -B -c "import json;from pathlib import Path;from harness.q2_stage1 import glmm,records as R;recs=R.read_jsonl(Path('$A/a1.jsonl'));p=json.load(open('$PLAN'));b={int(k):v for k,v in p['extension_blocks'].items()};f=R.final_records(recs);glmm.write_csv(glmm.rows_from_records(f,p['base']),Path('$A/glmm-inputs/primary.csv'));glmm.write_csv(glmm.rows_from_records(f,p['base']+[t for k in R.completed_extension_blocks(recs,b) for t in b[k]]),Path('$A/glmm-inputs/secondary.csv'))"
IMGG=sha256:b15584f3954f1c83fc3e5067e29c57c5c55e3b2a50ef28e4e68a394e595aabed
HEXG=$(python3 -c 'import json;print(json.dumps(["sh","-c","cp /opt/q2/r-packages.json /opt/q2/r-packages.sha256 /out/ && for f in primary secondary; do Rscript /src/harness/q2_stage1/glmm.R /inputs/$f.csv /out/glmm-$f.json 200 42 >/out/$f.log 2>&1 & done; wait"]).encode().hex())')
sbatch --parsable --export=ALL,Q2M_MODE=run,Q2M_IMAGE_ID=$IMGG,Q2M_ARGV_JSON_HEX=$HEXG,Q2M_SOURCE=$X,Q2M_RUN_DIR=$A/glmm-out,Q2M_INPUTS=$A/glmm-inputs $X/infra/slurm/host-single-node/s1a-cpu.sbatch
# About 15 min for the primary fit and 20 min for the secondary. Report full and reduced ok/pdHess as they are; if the full fit did not converge, say the bootstrap CIs come from that fit and include non-converged refits (bug 7).

# 8. Assemble the section 15 items the report lacks (bug 6), each stated as an operator step:
#    DR0 per job from step 1; host snapshots and foreign load from each lane-receipt.json 'snapshots';
#    plan['offline_excluded'] with reasons; losses by task, restarts per episode, output tokens, and
#    step-of-termination/success distributions from a1.jsonl final records; failed setup replies and
#    postconfig failures by type; the cost card against PRICE_CENTRAL (0.009020 at V=20) and PRICE_HIGH
#    (0.011274); the secondary set under corrected verdicts; rescoring coverage from step 2; the
#    'not externally anchored' label; every deviation (including any made for bugs 1-7).

# 9. Evidence and verification. Copy to program/evidence only metadata, counts, digests, receipts,
#    dr0-*.json, costs.json, report.json, first-divergence.json and glmm-*.json (no step logs, captures
#    or stdout tails; section 16). An independent verifier re-runs steps 3-7 from inputs.sha256 and
#    compares the sha256 of report.json, costs.json and the merged files.
